[ORIGINAL TEXT]: Lightweight Image SR Models. Recent years have been rising interest in investigating lightweight image SR models. These approaches try to design lightweight architectures, which mainly take advantage of recursive learning and channel splitting. Kim et al . ﬁrstly introduced recursive learning in DRCN to decrease model size (Kim et al., 2016b). Ahn et al . designed a cascading mechanism upon a residual network in CARN (Ahn et al., 2018). Hui et al . proposed a lightweight information multi-distillation network (IMDN) (Hui et al., 2019). Luo et al . designed the lattice block with butterﬂy structures (Luo et al., 2020). Recently, neural architecture search was introduced for image SR in FALSR (Chu et al., 2019a). Besides, model compression techniques, like knowledge distillation, have been investigated for image SR. He et al . proposed knowledge distillation based feature-afﬁnity for efﬁcient image SR (He et al., 2020). Lee et al . trained a  teacher network to distill its knowledge to a student  (Lee et al., 2020). Although those lightweight networks have achieved great progress,  we still need to investigate deeper for more efﬁcient image SR models.

[INSTRUCTION]: Use shorter formulations and more direct language to make the paragraph more concise.

[ANSWER]: Lightweight image SR models have gained popularity in recent years, focusing on designing compact architectures leveraging recursive learning and channel splitting. Kim et al. (2016b) introduced recursive learning in DRCN to reduce model size, while Ahn et al. (2018) designed a cascading mechanism in CARN. Hui et al. (2019) proposed a lightweight IMDN, and Luo et al. (2020) designed lattice blocks with butterfly structures. Neural architecture search was applied in FALSR (Chu et al., 2019a), and model compression techniques like knowledge distillation were investigated. He et al. (2020) proposed feature-affinity-based knowledge distillation, and Lee et al. (2020) trained a teacher network to distill knowledge to a student. Despite progress, more efficient image SR models are still needed.
